customer_acme_admin: Hey @support_jen — our GitHub SSO flow started failing today for some users. They finish the GitHub auth page and get redirected back, but our app logs a 'state mismatch' and login fails.

support_jen: Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro (steps + headers) and a sample of the redirect URL you received? Also confirm whether this is GitHub.com or GitHub Enterprise behind a proxy.

customer_acme_admin: It's GitHub Enterprise (on prem) behind a reverse proxy (F5). Repro steps: 1) Click "Login with GitHub" from mobile-web 2) redirect to GH login 3) after approve, GH redirects to our callback: 
```
GET /auth/callback?code=abc123&state=xyz%252F123%25AB HTTP/1.1
Host: login.acme.example
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
Referer: https://gh-enterprise.acme/callback
```
We store state when starting the flow as `xyz/123%AB` (raw, unescaped). When the callback arrives the state param appears double-percent-encoded: `xyz%252F123%25AB`. Our server decodes once and compares and it doesn't match stored value -> state mismatch.

support_jen: Thanks — that looks like the proxy is percent-encoding `%` again (so `%` -> `%25`). Can you grep access logs for the original outgoing redirect (the one we sent to GH) and the incoming callback to see the state forms? Also any proxy rewrite rules?

customer_acme_admin: I pulled logs. Outgoing redirect we issued: `Location: https://gh-enterprise.acme/authorize?state=xyz/123%AB&code_challenge=...` Incoming callback we see at our edge: `?state=xyz%252F123%25AB`. We checked F5 rules and found an iRule that normalizes query parts and re-encodes reserved chars.

eng_lina: Heads-up from infra: some proxies (and load balancers) will re-encode `Location`/`Referer` components or canonicalize query strings — double-encoding happens when the proxy percent-encodes an already-encoded value. Two quick workarounds to test: 1) encode state using base64url so it contains only url-safe characters (no `%`) and 2) make server comparison tolerant by normalizing both sides with a conservative decode loop (e.g., while contains `%25` replace with `%` then decode once).

support_jen: @customer_acme_admin can you try a quick experiment: generate a state token on client and base64url encode it before redirect; if callback comes back OK then we know proxy encoding was the issue. If you can't change client, we can do server-side normalization as a temporary band-aid.

customer_acme_admin: We're onboarding a bunch of SSO users tomorrow so we tried server-side normalization. Implemented a decode loop that decodes until there are no `%25` sequences, then compare. That made the immediate repros pass. But I'm worried about security implications / replay vectors.

security_omar: Good point. Normalizing is reasonable as a temporary mitigation but we should be careful: state must remain high-entropy and single-use. Normalizing encoded values is okay if you only canonicalize for comparison and still enforce nonce single-use and expiry. Don't accept additional variants beyond decoding — i.e., normalize deterministically, then compare to stored nonce and immediately mark it consumed. Also log original and normalized forms for a short retention window for investigation.

eng_lina: We'll triage a longer-term fix. Options: 1) Add a tolerant normalization path in the OAuth stack that will handle percent-percent-encoded states (with telemetry and opt-in flag); 2) Add guidance in docs about using base64url-safe state tokens for customers behind proxies; 3) Add a platform-side toggle for preserving raw query encoding when proxying (depends on gateway capabilities).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: oauth-normalize-patch -> staging (id: d-8032)

support_jen: Thanks @eng_lina and @security_omar. @customer_acme_admin — we'll push a staged fix to normalize callbacks in a restricted way to reduce immediate customer impact and follow-up with a docs/guide. Can you share request IDs for a few failing attempts so we can correlate logs?

customer_acme_admin: Sent three request IDs in DM. Also opened a support ticket with F5 team — they confirmed an iRule that canonicalizes query strings. They're planning a config change but it's scheduled for next week. The temporary normalization is fine for now but please push telemetry so we can see how many users are impacted.

eng_lina: Copy. We'll enable extra logging for those normalized states and emit a metric `oauth.state_normalized` with labels (customer, flow, proxy_detected) for 72h. We'll also add an opt-in config flag so we don't alter behavior by default.

security_omar: Recommend product notify customers in the tenant settings about the risk and suggest base64url encoding state in their next SDK versions.

support_jen: Closing the Slack loop — patch to staging applied, logging enabled. If problems persist once F5 change rolls out next week, we'll coordinate rolling back normalization. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

customer_acme_admin: Thanks — confirmed workaround fixed our test users. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

support_jen: Marking ticket as 'escalated->eng-infra' and adding postmortem checklist item: "document proxy double-encoding failure mode and recommended state encoding pattern (base64url)"
